# `plot.skyscapeR.horizon()` {#fn-plot-skyscaper-horizon}

W01 checked the skyline ordinate and azimuth viewport on flat and raised profiles, including natural and publication sky overlays. [W01 results](w01-plot-geometry.qmd).

[Function index](function-index.html#idx-plot-skyscaper-horizon)

```{=html}
<p>A track meeting the horizon identifies a possible rise or set direction for that
declination. The horizontal axis is true bearing and the vertical axis is angular
altitude. The function fills the terrain below the stored profile and can overlay
diurnal tracks computed for the observing location. Refraction affects those tracks.
Rescaling the display or changing its colours does not change the underlying horizon. Add lines or polygons in azimuth and altitude immediately after plotting. Set <code>par(mfrow=c(2,1))</code> before plotting to stack two horizons.
</p>
<p>For a two-year epoch range, draw tracks for the stored minimum and maximum
declinations, using the session refraction setting for both tracks. Line
styles are taken from the target object; older objects without them use
solid lines of width 1.
</p>
```

[Shading and numerical altitude](fn-dempalettes.qmd).

```{=html}
<table><thead><tr><th>Argument</th><th>Formal default</th><th>Behaviour in this interface</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><th scope="row"><code>x</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>Object of <em>skyscapeR.horizon</em> format.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>show.az</code></th><td><code>(!missing(xrange) || !missing(xlim))</code></td><td><p>Logical that controls whether to display azimuth values or cardinal
directions. Defaults to TRUE when xrange is supplied.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>xrange</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>Azimuth range for plotting.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>yrange</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>Altitude range for plotting. By default one degree of altitude occupies the same distance as one degree of azimuth on the device.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>obj</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>A <em>skyscapeR.object</em> from <code>skyObject</code>, or
a list of these objects. Each group retains its own epochs and styles
for displaying the paths of celestial objects.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>col.ground</code></th><td><code>NULL</code></td><td><p>Silhouette colour. NULL uses a dark muted foreground for natural skies, pale grey-green for publication colour or grey for monochrome.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>col.sky</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>Earlier name for a solid sky colour. Prefer sky.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>use.image</code></th><td><code>TRUE</code></td><td><p>Use an attached external panorama PNG when available. Default TRUE.
Missing or changed files warn and fall back to the numerical silhouette.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>...</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>Additional arguments to be passed to <em>plot</em>.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>show.skyline</code></th><td><code>NULL</code></td><td><p>Draw the numerical skyline. By default the line appears only without a panorama PNG.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>sky</code></th><td><code>NULL</code></td><td><p>A colour string or a background from <code>sketchSky</code> or <code>stellariumSky</code>.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>xlim</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>Earlier name for xrange.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>ylim</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>Earlier name for yrange.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>fastLoad</code></th><td><code>FALSE</code></td><td><p>Use a sampled PNG for quick plots. New photographic imports store a preview. For older horizons the first preview loads the image. The numerical skyline and celestial tracks retain their precision.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>show.legend</code></th><td><code>TRUE</code></td><td><p>Display the key for celestial tracks. The angular axes are always drawn.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>style</code></th><td><code>NULL</code></td><td><p>Frame and silhouette style. A sketch supplies its stored style by default. Without a
sketch the default is <code>"publication-colour"</code>. Other choices are <code>"natural"</code> and
<code>"publication-mono"</code>. Supplied panorama pixels and sky objects retain their own rendering.</p></td></tr></tbody></table><h5>Return value</h5><p>Draws the horizon and returns the session atmosphere invisibly in a list.
</p><h5>Layers and coordinate consistency</h5><p>A reusable sky is calculated for its own stored location and instant. Pair it
with the horizon used to create it; drawing a saved sky does not recalculate
its positions for another observer. Celestial reference tracks from
<code>skyObject</code> use the plotted horizon's location and session
atmosphere. Keep that atmosphere consistent with the stored sketch when
comparing a track with a disc or point symbol.
</p><p>The foreground masks sky layers geometrically. It does not make the sky object
an extinction or visibility calculation through the terrain. Image calibration
and numerical skyline agreement remain the responsibility of the horizon
source. Azimuth-altitude plotting is a cylindrical display, with increasing
horizontal distortion towards the zenith. Retain consistent ranges when
comparing styles, epochs or constellation traditions.
</p>
```

</details>
